content: 1. Conjugated synthetic estrogens can have their levels or effects increased by DHEA (a herbal supplement) through modulation of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Diltiazem increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by weak-to-moderate induction of CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A4 substrates if needed. 7. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates when co-administered. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Ertapenem decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora, but also increases their levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. These interactions apply only to oral hormone forms and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora, but also increases their levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. These interactions apply only to oral hormone forms and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora, but also increases their levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. These interactions apply only to oral hormone forms and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora, but also increases their levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. These interactions apply only to oral hormone forms and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of exemestane through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens or estrogen-containing products, including combined oral contraceptives, should not be co-administered with exemestane as they may interfere with its pharmacologic action and efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Felodipine increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Fleroxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Fosfomycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Gentamicin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may decrease the efficacy of hemin. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of hyaluronidase by rendering tissues partially resistant to its action when administered in large systemic doses. Patients may require larger amounts of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Iloperidone increases the levels of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 35. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of insulin degludec, insulin degludec/aspart, and inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 37. Conjugated synthetic estrogens decrease the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. At 40 mg/day, istradefylline increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Conjugated synthetic estrogens decrease the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Lapatinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last SC dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Conjugated synthetic estrogens increase the levels or effects of linagliptin by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended when linagliptin is to be administered with a CYP3A4 inducer. Caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Linezolid decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 48. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. Conjugated synthetic estrogens decrease the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 response. Patients receiving oral estrogen replacement may require higher lonapegsomatropin dosages. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 51. Loratadine increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 52. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 53. Conjugated synthetic estrogens increase the levels of maraviroc by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 55. Meropenem decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Meropenem/vaborbactam decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 57. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 58. Methylprednisolone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 59. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora, but also increases their levels or effects by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions apply only to oral hormone forms and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 60. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 61. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 62. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 63. Mitotane decreases the levels of conjugated synthetic estrogens by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitoring is necessary when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Caution and monitoring are advised.
